n: While still confined in the guard courtyard, Jeremiah receives a second message continuing the promises of chapter 32.
The message comes from the Lord who made, shaped, and established the earth—and who will establish his promises too.
“Call to me and I will answer, and show you great and hidden things you do not know.” A beloved invitation to prayer and revelation.

f.w: Call unto me, and I will answer thee

f.g: Hebrew betsurot—fortified, inaccessible things; secrets only God can unlock.

n: God speaks about Jerusalem’s houses and royal buildings, torn down to strengthen the walls against siege ramps and swords.

f.g: Houses were demolished to get materials to reinforce walls against siege ramps.

n: The defenders fight on, but only fill those houses with corpses, because God has hidden his face from the city’s wickedness.
Yet God will heal the city and its people and reveal to them abundant peace and truth.

f.w: I will bring it health and cure

n: He will bring back the captives of both Judah and Israel and rebuild them as at the beginning.
He will cleanse them from all their sins and forgive every rebellion. Restoration of land comes with forgiveness of heart.

f.w: I will cleanse them from all their iniquity

n: Jerusalem will bring God joy, praise, and honor before all nations, who will tremble in awe at the good he does for her.
Again in this place—now called a wasteland without people or animals—there will be sound…

…the sounds of joy, weddings, and worshippers bringing thank offerings and singing, “Praise the Lord, for he is good; his mercy endures forever.” The very sounds silenced in 7:34 and 25:10 will return.

f.w: the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride
for his mercy endureth for ever

n: Shepherds will again rest their flocks in pastures throughout this now-empty land.
In every region of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hand of the one counting them—an image of peaceful, ordered life. Christians also see the Good Shepherd who knows each sheep.

f.g: Telleth = counts. Shepherds counted sheep as they passed under the rod.

n: The days are coming when God will fulfill the good promise he made to Israel and Judah.
He will make a righteous “Branch” sprout from David’s line, who will do justice and righteousness in the land—repeating the messianic promise of 23:5.
Judah will be saved and Jerusalem safe. This time the name “The LORD our righteousness” is given to the city itself—the people take on the character of their King.
David will never lack a descendant to sit on Israel’s throne. Christians understand this to be fulfilled in Jesus Christ, the eternal King from David’s line.

f.w: David shall never want a man

n: Nor will the Levite priests ever lack someone to offer sacrifices before God. Latter-day Saints see a latter-day fulfillment in the restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood and the prophecy of an offering by the sons of Levi.
Another word from the Lord comes to Jeremiah.
If you could break God’s “covenant” with day and night so that they didn’t come on schedule…

f.w: my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night

n: …only then could his covenant with David and with the Levitical priests be broken.
Just as stars and sand can’t be counted, God will multiply David’s descendants and the Levites who serve him—echoing his promise to Abraham.

f.w: As the host of heaven cannot be numbered

n: The Lord speaks again to Jeremiah.
Have you heard people saying God has rejected the two families he chose (Israel and Judah, or the royal and priestly lines)? They treat God’s people with contempt, as if no longer a nation.
God replies: only if I had not established day and night and the laws of heaven and earth…
…would I reject Jacob’s descendants and David’s line. But I will restore them and have mercy on them. God’s covenant faithfulness is as certain as the sunrise.

f.w: I will cause their captivity to return
